Questions decompose the sklearn feature selector enhancement requirement into concrete user context, use-case drivers, and success definitions.

Generated 9 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (group-based CV necessity), pain points (current SequentialFeatureSelector limitations), and acceptance criteria (transparent groups propagation, validation, test scenarios). Questions decompose the requirement into workflow context, data characteristics, integration points, validation strategy, and prioritization—grounding dialogue in the sklearn_2021q4 case.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (group-based CV workflows), pain points (current workarounds), and acceptance criteria (groups parameter propagation through SequentialFeatureSelector call chain). Questions probe concrete use cases, stakeholder impact, and prioritization to ground requirements in measurable acceptance conditions.

End user requires group-based cross-validation support in SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() to handle grouped datasets (medical/temporal data) and maintain sklearn API consistency. Current limitation forces workarounds. Solution: add optional groups parameter flowing through to cross_val_score().

End-user requires SequentialFeatureSelector to support group-based cross-validation via an optional groups parameter in fit() to handle non-independent data scenarios (grouped datasets, time-series, multi-sample subjects) while maintaining API consistency with sklearn standards and backward compatibility.

End-user requires SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() to accept an optional groups parameter for group-based cross-validation to handle non-independent data and resolve API inconsistency with sklearn's standard cross-validation pattern, while maintaining backward compatibility.

Clarification questions address groups parameter semantics (handling with different cv types), validation strategy (length matching, error timing), backward compatibility (explicit None vs. omission), pipeline propagation (transformers vs. estimators), documentation scope (iteration coverage), failure modes (validation timing), and performance considerations (caching across iterations).

Six clarification questions raised regarding groups parameter behavior with different cv configurations, validation timing/strictness, backward compatibility semantics, and internal API propagation strategy to ensure consistent sklearn API patterns and clear error handling for group-based cross-validation in SequentialFeatureSelector.

Six clarification questions raised by EndUser to resolve ambiguities in groups parameter design: (1) interaction with string cv values, (2) validation responsibility allocation, (3) backward compatibility semantics, (4) propagation through internal methods, (5) edge cases with None cv, (6) type validation expectations. These clarifications are critical for defining the complete API contract and ensuring consistent behavior across sklearn's cross-validation infrastructure.

End-user requirements validated and refined. Groups parameter must be added to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() as optional, backward-compatible, and delegating validation to cross_val_score(). Behavior when cv is a string or groups=None is clarified to match sklearn conventions.

End-user requirement validated and refined: SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() must accept optional groups parameter to enable group-based cross-validation for non-independent data. Validation deferred to cross_val_score() per sklearn convention. Backward-compatible with no special handling for string cv values. Implementation chain confirmed: fit() → _get_best_new_feature() → cross_val_score().

End-user requirements validated: SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() must add an optional, backward-compatible groups parameter flowing through to cross_val_score(). Three clarifications remain regarding interaction with string cv values, validation responsibility, and None-handling semantics.

Consolidated 10 structured elicitation records addressing the addition of an optional groups parameter to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() for group-based cross-validation support. Requirements establish functional flow through internal methods, enforce backward compatibility, delegate validation to cross_val_score(), and clarify behavior across cv parameter types (string, integer, custom splitter). All records align with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and reflect confirmed end-user pain points (API inconsistency, non-independent data handling) and validated expectations (optional, backward-compatible, standard sklearn pattern).

Eight prioritized user requirements synthesized from interview records and enduser confirmations. Core MUST requirements establish groups parameter acceptance, propagation through call chain, backward compatibility, and delegation of validation to cross_val_score(). SHOULD requirements address quality concerns around validation responsibility and documentation clarity. COULD requirement addresses user education to reduce API confusion. All requirements trace to confirmed pain points (API inconsistency, non-independent data support) and validated expectations (sklearn pattern alignment, backward compatibility).

Targeted interviewer questions probe Deployer's infrastructure constraints (environment topology, sklearn versioning, scalability limits), security mandates (groups metadata handling, privacy governance), validation delegation model (error-handling expectations vs. cross_val_score() responsibility), backward-compatibility rollout strategy, integration patterns (serialization, monitoring), and performance budgets. Chain-of-Thought reasoning: (1) Identify deployment context (environments, versions, scale), (2) Clarify validation ownership and error-handling expectations, (3) Probe backward-compatibility rollout mechanics and legacy code impact, (4) Explore integration touchpoints (persistence, observability), (5) Validate performance and security constraints on parameter propagation.

Probing Deployer on infrastructure topology, security validation mandates, scalability constraints, error-handling responsibility allocation, backward-compatibility verification procedures, CV-groups interaction semantics, Pipeline integration requirements, and validation delegation tolerance to align implementation with operational deployment realities.

Chain-of-Thought: The Deployer must clarify infrastructure constraints (scale, environment, multi-tenancy), security mandates (data governance, audit logging), scalability expectations (group validation overhead, performance thresholds), and validation responsibility delegation (early vs. deferred). Ten targeted questions probe deployment readiness, backward compatibility risk, and error-handling strategy to ensure the groups parameter addition aligns with production requirements and operational constraints.

Infrastructure deployment of groups parameter addition to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() requires minimal constraints: optional parameter with None default ensures backward compatibility and zero breaking changes; delegate all validation to cross_val_score() per sklearn convention; negligible memory/latency overhead; no new security surface; existing CI/CD pipelines unaffected; phased rollout supported; long-term maintenance simplified through single-responsibility principle.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness: Python 3.7+ with scikit-learn ≥0.24; groups parameter adds negligible overhead (<1KB, O(n) reference passing); security validation delegated to cross_val_score() per sklearn pattern; scalability unaffected for million-sample datasets; backward compatibility guaranteed through optional parameter with None default; operational procedures follow sklearn convention of silent group parameter passing to non-group-aware splitters.

Deploy groups parameter support to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() with Python 3.7+/scikit-learn ≥0.24; groups is reference-passed through call chain with O(n) overhead only; validation delegated to cross_val_score() per sklearn convention; full backward compatibility with zero infrastructure/cost impact; silent pass-through for non-group-aware splitters; supports millions of samples without scalability penalty.

Deployer raises six clarifications on groups parameter validation boundaries, sklearn version compatibility, performance optimization trade-offs, backward compatibility edge cases, API signature alignment with sklearn standards, and memory footprint validation under recursive call scenarios. Requires explicit confirmation before implementation to prevent deployment conflicts and ensure consistency with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 infrastructure checklist requirements.

Five clarifications needed on groups parameter validation responsibility, sklearn cross-version compatibility, performance optimization for large datasets, explicit vs. omitted None semantics, and untrusted input security boundaries. These directly impact implementation strategy, error-handling design, and deployment compatibility scope.

Infrastructure requirements (Python 3.7+, scikit-learn ≥0.24) are stable and widely available. Deployment cleared for implementation.
